gap: No result ChatGPT got states the Keychron Q1 Max's 22.6 mm front height and fixed 5.2° typing angle, which is the height a low-profile board is meant to remove; I could not get a named reviewer's own measurement for any of the candidates.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and got no results in either chat, so there are no rival pages to compare against. Its tables only say low-profile boards 'usually' cause 'less wrist extension' and that standard boards 'may benefit from a wrist rest', with no numbers. Against that, any measured figure would be new. But the only figure I could open is Keychron's own spec, reprinted by KitGuru, and not a lab measurement. RTINGS has measured all of these boards, but its figures are members-only.
decides: It partly supports ChatGPT's 'standard mechanical may need a wrist rest' line: the Q1 Max stands 22.6 mm at the front before keycaps, and its 5.2° angle can't be changed. Without a measured height, noise level or latency for the NuPhy Air75 V2, Keychron K3 Max or Lofree Flow 2, it doesn't change the pick between low-profile and full-height. A side-by-side table of named measurements can't be built from pages I could open.
